julie (Customer): Hey, submitting the form on the dashboard returns a blank page and nothing in the UI. I see a 500 in the network tab and some CORS/auth noise in the console. Happening in Chrome on macOS.

sarah (Support): Sorry about that — can you grab a quick HAR + console dump so we can see request/response and any console errors? Also share the X-Request-ID from the failed request if present.

julie (Customer): How do I get the HAR and the request ID?

sarah (Support): Quick steps (Chrome / Edge):
1) Open DevTools (Cmd+Option+I) -> Network tab.
2) Check "Preserve log" at top so requests persist.
3) Reproduce the error (submit the form).
4) Right-click anywhere in the Network panel -> "Save all as HAR with content" -> save.
5) Console tab: right-click -> "Save as..." or copy errors.

For Firefox:
- DevTools -> Network -> gear -> enable "Persist logs" -> reproduce -> right click -> "Save all as HAR".

Also look at the failing request in Network and click the Headers tab. If there is a header like `x-request-id` or `request-id` or `x-rw-request-id`, copy that value and paste here. If you see an error body, copy it too.

matt (DevEx): If you want a single bundle: after saving HAR, go to Console, select messages (Ctrl/Cmd+A) -> right click -> "Save as" -> attach both files. If you're comfortable pasting, include the failing request's response body and the request payload (Headers -> Request Payload).

julie (Customer): Got the HAR and console. The request shows status 500 and header `x-request-id: c9f3e8d2-11b4-4a6a-b7d2`. Attached har and console.txt.

infra-bot: Debug bundle received: upload token ABC123 (expires in 1h).

sarah (Support): Thanks — next steps for us:
- We'll search logs for that request id `c9f3e8d2-11b4-4a6a-b7d2`.
- If we need a curl repro, we'll ask for the request method, URL, headers (esp Authorization, X-Request-ID), and body.

matt (DevEx): If you want to generate a curl from the HAR quickly, you can: open the HAR in a viewer (or use a small script). Example curl (replace token and body):

```bash
curl 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/submit' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>' 
  -H 'x-request-id: c9f3e8d2-11b4-4a6a-b7d2' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  --data-raw '{"name":"Julie","payload":{...}}' 
  -v
```

Note: remove any real PII before pasting. If the failure is auth-related, ensure your token isn't expired; we can check server-side if you send the request id.

julie (Customer): Upload link has expired when I tried.

infra-bot: New upload token DEF456 created by sarah (expires in 1h).

sarah (Support): Re-upload using the token link and reply here when it's done. If upload fails, you can paste the failing request/response bodies masked for secrets.

julie (Customer): Re-uploaded — link: https://uploads.redwood.internal/debug/DEF456. HAR and console attached.

sarah (Support): Received. We found a 500 trace with that request id and a stackframe pointing to auth/session refresh. Can you confirm whether you were using SSO or API key?

julie (Customer): SSO via SAML. We just rotated credentials last night but UI login worked.

matt (DevEx): Useful extra things to include if we need more:
- Steps to reproduce (exact buttons, env: prod/staging).
- Time window when you reproduced (we'll correlate).
- Screenshot of Network Headers showing Authorization header masked.

sarah (Support): We'll follow up after we review the service logs. If we decide to ask for a minimal curl repro, we'll provide an example payload that preserves request shape but scrubs secrets.

julie (Customer): Thanks, appreciate the quick help. :pray:

sarah (Support): No problem — looping in eng if needed. @matt can you take a look at the trace when you have a sec?

matt (DevEx): On it — downloading HAR now. :mag: 

sarah (Support): Marking this thread as triaged. We'll post updates here once we confirm root cause or need more info. :white_check_mark:
